To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified the proteins in a sample of cells prepared by laser capture of a breast cancer line (SKBR-3).

the combination of laser capture microdissections, protein extraction and digestion and mass spectrometric analysis of peptides can be used to identify proteins from a small number of cells and that this approach may have potential applications in clinical studies.
the proteomics of a breast cancer (SKBR‐ 3) cell line was successfully performed on a limited sample (approximately 10 000 cells) prepared by LCM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of proteins in a cell line that has been isolated from a tissue sample by LCM.
the development of methods for the proteomic analysis and identification of proteins in selected cells.
the development of a methodology for proteomic analysis of selected tissue samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study demonstrated that it is feasible to use LCM to isolate a small number of cells from a cell line, solubilize the proteins in these cells, digest the proteins and perform proteomic analysis on the resulting peptide mixture by LC/MS.
this study has shown that it is feasible to perform proteomic studies on small numbers of cells isolated by LCM.
this study has demonstrated the feasibility of the approach and the potential of such studies for future applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proteomic analysis on a single sample of laser microdissected cells allowed the identification of a large number of proteins, which are involved in the metastatic process of breast cancer cells.
this approach allowed the identification of a number of proteins that have previously been implicated in cancer, as well as a number of proteins not previously identified.
the proteomic analysis on laser captured SKBR‐3 cells allowed the identification of 26 proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of the laser capture microdissected cells with a single step protein extraction and trypsin digestion allowed for the successful analysis of the proteome of the captured cell population.
the LCM approach is a powerful tool for proteomic analysis and the approach is applicable to the analysis of proteins in a wide range of cell types.
it demonstrates that it is possible to perform a proteomic study on a small number of cells.
